title: Traffic guardrails and hybrid canary notebook (working)
content:
Purpose

This is a working notebook for a hybrid canary + A/B testing approach that combines: staged user canaries, synthetic traffic validation, and small-cohort A/B experiments. The goal is a single lightweight playbook product and ops teams can use for low-risk LLM feature rollouts (rerankers, new prompt templates, model variants, caching changes).

High-level constraints and goals (non-exhaustive)
- Keep customer-facing latency and error budget intact (SLOs should be preserved).
- Minimize cost blowups when enabling higher-quality but more expensive model variants.
- Detect regressions in quality and hallucination rates quickly (within the first 30–60 minutes for visible traffic slices).
- Provide automated fallback and clear manual reversion paths.
- Make the experiment spec concise enough for on-call to review in 5 minutes.

Core components of the hybrid flow
1) Dry-run synthetic validation (pre-rollout)
   - Replay a representative recent traffic sample through the candidate change in a private environment.
   - Synthetic checks: token rate, per-request latency distribution, 95/99th percentiles, memory/kvcache growth, error rates (model timeouts, OOM).
   - Quality checks: embed+cosine similarity on a reference set of 500 prompts (quick pass/fail thresholds).
   - Cost sanity: estimated per-1k requests token cost compared to baseline (warn if > 2x).

2) Micro-canary (0.05% — 0.5% traffic)
   - Live traffic routed to candidate variant in shadow or active mode depending on change type.
   - Observability: latency histograms, error counts, throttles, per-route token counts.
   - Telemetry to watch: user-visible errors, UI-timeout events, spike in retry loops, and degradation in key downstream metrics (CTR, conversion).

3) Cohorted A/B experiment (1% — 10%)
   - Run a short A/B with clear hypothesis, primary metric, and guardrail metrics.
   - Duration: min 24h, recommended 72h for low-signal features.
   - If cost-sensitive, limit to off-hours windows first or synthetic heavy users only.

4) Gradual ramp to target (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
   - Each step must pass guardrail checks for a stability window (default 60 minutes stable, configurable).
   - If any guardrail trips, automatic rollback to previous stable variant.

Guardrail metrics and thresholds (suggested defaults)
- Latency: 95th percentile should not increase by more than +30% vs baseline; 99th percentile not more than +50% (for high-sensitivity routes tighten these numbers).
- Error rate: 5xxs or model timeouts increase must be <= +0.1 percentage points absolute and <= 10% relative.
- Quality regressions: this is model/feature-specific; we require a small prompt-set pass/fail: e.g., A->B BLEU-like or similarity drop not > 3 points (or custom eval metric).
- Operational alarms: increase in retry loops, token usage anomalies (sudden +200% tokens per request), or per-route cost increase beyond configured budget (trigger).
- Business signals: primary product KPI (CTR, revenue per session) should not drop more than X% — X defined per-experiment. If not defined, default to 5% relative drop.

Autopolicies (automatic actions)
- Soft-fail: notify stakeholders and pause ramp (do not rollback) when a single non-critical metric breaches.
- Hard-fail: immediate rollback when critical alarms fire (e.g., increased 5xx > threshold for 10m, or token cost > 2x and ongoing).
- Throttle fallback: reduce candidate variant traffic by half and hold for double the stability window if noisy signals appear.

Experiment spec template (minimal fields)
- title: Short descriptive name
- owner: Product/engineer oncall
- start-window: YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm (timezone)
- hypothesis: 1-2 sentence statement
- primary-kpi: metric + direction + measurement window
- guardrails: list of metrics with thresholds (latency, errors, cost, custom eval)
- traffic-slices: slices and allocation plan (e.g., 0.05% global, 50% internal users, 49.95% control)
- rollback-criteria: explicit conditions (auto and manual)
- communication: slack channel + escalation list
- rollback-owner: who is accountable if auto rollback fails

Operator checklist (pre-activation)
- [ ] Confirm synthetic validation pass (attach logs).
- [ ] Confirm canary traffic slice is instrumented in dashboard.
- [ ] Confirm runbook link and Slack alert channel in experiment config.
- [ ] Confirm budget alarm set (cost threshold).
- [ ] Notify CS for any customers on dedicated/dedicated-with-private data paths.

Operator checklist (during ramp)
- [ ] T+15m quick sanity: latency + errors glance
- [ ] T+60m stability window: confirm no guardrail breaches
- [ ] Post 24h: check primary KPI and quality eval results

Post-release artifacts
- Short postmortem note (if rollback): what tripped, how resolved, candidate actions to harden.
- If successful: short performance / cost delta summary + next steps (fully roll or run extended A/B).

Communication templates (Slack)
- Activation: "Rolling canary: <experiment-name> started at <time>. Owner: <owner>. Slack: <channel>. Guardrails set: latency + errors + cost. Please monitor dashboard <link>."
- Hard-fail alert: "AUTO-ROLLBACK: <experiment-name> rolled back at <time>. Trigger: <metric> exceeded threshold. Investigating: <oncall>. Postmortem: <link>"

Examples of tricky cases (notes to self)
- Model quantization change: good synthetic latency wins, but may subtly change hallucination profile. Need to add hallucination-specific signals (hallucination detectors or manual evals on a small sample).
- Cost/quality tradeoffs: interactive features sometimes need dynamic gating (e.g., use expensive model only after prefix matched). Consider per-route dynamic routing via console flags.
- Dedicated customers: must surface rollout plan in the customer tenancy dashboard and get explicit approval if memory/KV cache changes are involved.

Observability implementation notes
- Dashboards: per-route breakdown, candidate vs control overlays, token-cost per request, streaming latencies, KV cache hit/miss ratios.
- Traces: sample full trace for any slow or error request hitting canary variant.
- Eval pipeline: automated batch eval that runs nightly on canary-produced outputs and pushes pass/fail to experiment dashboard.

Open questions / TODOs
- [ ] What is the canonical short prompt-set for quick quality pass for each product area? Define owners.
- [ ] How to encode cost budgets per experiment so console can automatically create cost alarms? (product + finance)
- [ ] Should we add a "confidence weight" per metric used in autopolicies so marginal breaches by low-confidence signals don't hard-fail?
- [ ] Integrate with Dedicated contract metadata so certain customers are excluded unless they opt-in.

Quick references and links
- Existing rollout policy notes: CONFLUENCE-ROLLUP (link above)
- Incident runbooks (SRE): CONFLUENCE-INC-ONCALL
- Experiment tracking proto (github): https://github.com/redwood/rollout-proto/pull/394

Last thoughts
This notebook should live close to the console product area docs (product/console-and-rollouts). The goal is to prototype a single UI flow that can generate an experiment spec from this template, wire in autopolicies, and present a compact operator surface for oncall to act on quickly.

If you are reading: add quick notes inline, mark TODOs, and if you create a follow-up PR on rollout-proto please reference JIRA-ROLL-78.

-- Maya
